text: . Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said that renewed diplomacy with Washington remains possible if the US changes its approach and abandons coercion. Mr Araghchi said in a social media post that the US should build trust, speak respectfully, acknowledge our rights, and uphold commitments. He also described recent talks with Qatar’s prime minister and foreign minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, as productive and creative.US President Donald Trump, however, ruled out immediate talks with Tehran and said American military operations against Iran may not be over. Trump said Iran was under severe military and economic pressure and had limited capabilities. He cautioned that the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz did not mean the US had ended its military engagement with Iran. Trump said there’s not a lot to speak with Iran; he also added that Washington was not looking to meet or anything. Trump also said Russia had so far behaved quite well regarding the Strait of Hormuz but did not specify any Russian commitments or actions toward Iran.

. The Tata Institute of Social Sciences, TISS, conferred degrees on 1,376 students and scholars at its 86th annual convocation held in Mumbai yesterday.The degrees included those awarded to 35 doctoral scholars and graduates from Master’s, Bachelor’s, Integrated and dual-degree programmes.The first undergraduate batch of Analytics and Sustainability Studies also received their degrees. Director of Tata Memorial Hospital, Dr C. S. Pramesh, was the chief guest at the convocation.

. All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi has introduced a new course titled GARBHINI MITRA to Strengthen Ayurveda-Based Maternal Wellness Support for the 2026-2027 academic session.The Ministry of AYUSH said that the six-month course is designed to develop trained personnel to provide appropriate health education, lifestyle guidance, and community-level support to women during pregnancy and the postnatal period.The ministry noted that Candidates of 18 years or above, who have passed the Senior Secondary examination from any recognized board are eligible to apply before its last date that is 31st August.Once completed, candidates can work as Garbhini Mitra Assistants, Prenatal or Postnatal Care Assistants, Antenatal Wellness Guides and Maternal Health Support Workers, across different Ayush centres, maternity clinics and wellness institutions.The course inculcates traditional ayurvedic concepts of Garbhini Paricharya, Sutika Paricharya and Garbhadhana Vidhi.

. A barrier lake formed near the confluence of the Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo rivers in Nepal could face a high risk of breaching over the next three days. According to the China’s Ministry of Water Resources, the lake held an estimated two million cubic metres of water as of today morning and was already overflowing. The ministry also warned that another three million cubic metres of water could enter the lake over the next three days, posing a high risk of a breach.China national daily reported that authorities are closely monitoring the situation while conducting flood simulations and risk assessments to prepare for a possible breach and facilitate emergency rescue operations. This comes as hundreds died and thousands remain missing after catastrophic flash floods in the China-Nepal border region.

. The Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC) today accused Pakistani security forces of enforced disappearances, arbitrary detentions, and forced evictions in the Shadi Kor area of Balochistan. In a statement, the rights organization alleged that in May this year, personnel from the Pakistani Army and Military Intelligence rounded up residents and detained a large number of people.The BYC claimed those detained were subjected to violence and degrading treatment, with around 40 people allegedly forcibly disappeared and taken to a military camp near the Shadi Kor Dam. According to the BYC, people returning home with food and other rations have been stopped at checkpoints, while road blockades have made it difficult for residents to obtain basic necessities. The Baloch rights group also called on international human rights organizations, United Nations bodies, and the international community to investigate the allegations.

. Norway’s King Harald V died today at 89 at a hospital in Oslo. Europe’s oldest monarch Harald became king in 1991 after the death of his father, King Olav V, and was widely popular for modernising the monarchy. He spent part of his childhood in exile in the United States after Nazi Germany invaded Norway during World War II. His son, Crown Prince Haakon, succeeds him as king.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed grief over the passing away of King Harald V of Norway. The Prime Minister recalled his meeting with King Harald V during his visit to Norway earlier this year. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that he was deeply touched by his warmth and profound sense of service to the nation. He also conveyed condolences to the Royal Family and the people of Norway.

. The Publications Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has received seven awards at the Federation of Indian Publishers (FIP) Awards for Excellence in Book Production, 2026. The Division’s journals, books and reference publications in Hindi, English and Urdu have been recognised in various categories.Director General, Publications Division, Dr. Dhiraj Kakadia said that the books and journals published by the Division play an important role in bringing diverse and valuable content related to national development, literature, culture, art and contemporary issues to readers. He said, the seven awards received by the Publications Division are a testament to the collective hard work, dedication and excellence of its officers and personnel.

. The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) has achieved a major milestone in its nationwide mission-mode drive for Mandatory Biometric Updates, completing more than two crore biometric updates for school children across the country. The special drive, initiated in September last year, has now covered over one lakh 56 thousand schools, enabling school children to complete their Aadhaar biometric. Electronics and IT Ministry said that this has helped Mandatory Biometric Updates service to reach children directly at their schools, making the process more accessible and convenient for crores of students.Aadhaar enrolment for children below five years captures demographic information and a photograph, while fingerprints and iris biometrics are not captured at that age as these biometrics are still developing. Mandatory Biometric Updates helps ensure that the child’s Aadhaar continues to have updated biometric information. The Biometric updates are required when a child attains the age of 5 years and again at 15 years. To encourage timely completion and make the service more accessible, UIDAI had waived the charges for  children in the 7 to 15 years age group from 1st October 2025, for a period of one year. The Ministry said that lack of Biometric Updates in Aadhaar may lead to difficulties while carrying out authentication for receiving benefits under various Government schemes, registering in competitive and university examinations.

. Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh today informed that around 440 space technology startups are registered in India. In a written reply in Lok Sabha, Dr Singh said Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre, IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities, NGEs to carry out various space activities. Out of these, 18 NGEs are start-ups. The Minister said the Government has undertaken several proactive measures following the liberalization of the space sector. This is being done to promote participation of startups in satellite manufacturing, launch services, downstream applications and space-based technologies. IN-SPACe is facilitating the transfer of available ISRO technologies to industry while also identifying and consolidating the technology requirements of industry for future technology development and transfer. Till date, 118 Technology Transfer Agreements have been executed.

. US lawmakers today reintroduced legislation aimed at tightening sanctions on China-based entities accused of supporting the production, trafficking and sale of fentanyl and its precursor chemicals. The bipartisan CCP Fentanyl Sanctions Act was reintroduced by the House Select Committee on China, as Washington steps up pressure on Beijing over its alleged role in America’s opioid crisis.The bill targets Chinese chemical manufacturers, online vendors and other entities accused of profiting from the illicit synthetic narcotics trade. It would allow sanctions against Chinese vessels and ports found to have knowingly or recklessly facilitated the transportation of illicit synthetic narcotics. Lawmakers also pointed to a 2024 Select Committee report, which alleged that the Chinese Communist Party subsidised the production of fentanyl precursor chemicals that were later sold to Mexican drug cartels.

. Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini honoured Commonwealth Games medallists and participants from Haryana at a state-level felicitation ceremony held in Panchkula today. Cash awards totalling ₹13 crore 97 lakh 50 thousand were presented to 24 athletes at the event.Expressing pride in the athletes’ achievements, the Chief Minister remarked that an athlete’s success is underpinned by the faith of their parents, the discipline instilled by their mentors, and the resolve to rise again after every defeat. He noted that India secured the fourth position on the medal tally at the 23rd Commonwealth Games, winning a total of 39 medals comprising 13 gold, 17 silver, and 9 bronze.Haryana once again distinguished itself during this glorious moment. He highlighted that while Haryana accounts for merely 2 percent of the country’s total population, athletes from the state clinched a total of 11 medals in these games.Commending the performance of the state’s daughters in particular, the Chief Minister pointed out that 6 of the 11 medals won by Haryana’s athletes were secured by women, including 5 gold medals. He expressed confidence that, driven by the prowess of its athletes, India would emerge as a global sporting powerhouse at the Olympic Games.

. External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that 320 Indian nationals remain uncontactable or are reportedly missing following the flash flood tragedy on Wednesday. He said, around 100 people of Indian origin, holding other nationalities, also remain uncontactable.Addressing the media in New Delhi today, Mr Jaiswal said that 63 Indian nationals working at the Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project were rescued from the affected area. He said, another 96 Indian nationals who were stranded on the Chinese side have safely crossed into Nepal by land and efforts are underway to evacuate them. Mr Jaiswal informed the media that twenty-one Indian nationals from Tamil Nadu, who had arrived in Kathmandu from the flood-affected area yesterday, have reached New Delhi this afternoon.On the Chinese side, Mr Jaiswal said that around 400 Indian nationals are safe and in contact with their families. He said, the Indian Embassy in Beijing is coordinating with local authorities, team leaders and travel agents to facilitate their evacuation.Meanwhile, India has stepped up humanitarian assistance to Nepal. Mr Jaiswal said that India has sent more than 47 tonnes of emergency relief supplies aimed at supporting Nepal’s ongoing rescue and relief operations. He informed that a third relief flight is expected to depart this evening, carrying around  13 tonnes of essential supplies, including portable generator sets, food, water purification tablets and medicines.Mr Jaiswal said that the government has set up a control room in the Ministry of External Affairs, which is working round the clock. He said Indian embassies, both in Kathmandu and Beijing, have also set up 24×7 helplines.

. India has launched a major rescue and relief operation following the Nepal flood flash. The External Affairs Ministry said 290 Indian nationals in Nepal remain uncontactable, with efforts underway to trace them and coordinate their rescue. So far, India has rescued 84 nationals, including 63 workers from the Trishuli-I run-of-river hydroelectric project and 21 people from Tamil Nadu. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said the ministry is coordinating with the Nepal government, other ministries, state governments, tour operators and relevant authorities. A 24-hour control room has also been established to assist with tracing and evacuation efforts. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and assured him of India’s full humanitarian assistance.

. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has voiced deep sadness over the severe flooding in Nepal and China that has caused widespread destruction. The international body allocated an initial tranche of two million US dollars for relief operations.The United Nations is supporting the government-led response in Nepal, including assessing the scale of the disaster and delivering urgent assistance. UN teams and humanitarian partners are mobilising supplies and personnel to support communities affected by the floods.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today discussed the relief and rescue efforts underway in Nepal today. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar said that the Indian Embassies in Kathmandu and Beijing provided an updated picture in respect of the status and well-being of Indian nationals. He also informed that the concerned Ministry of External Affairs Divisions have apprised about the further relief supplies to be sent to Nepal.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the Jan Dhan Yojana has delivered unprecedented scale and transformative outcomes, with an unparalleled impact in the last 12 years. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that Jan Dhan Yojana is playing a significant role in advancing financial inclusion and empowering people across the country. Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, more than 59 crore accounts have been opened so far, with total deposits amounting to 3 lakh 17 thousand crore rupees. The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Modi on this day in 2014. As the world’s largest financial inclusion initiative, the scheme continues to redefine access to banking for all Indians. Under the scheme, 78 per cent of the accounts have been opened in rural or semi-urban areas, and approximately 56 per cent of accounts are owned by women.

. The Government has debunked a fake video circulating in social media, falsely claiming that the wall of the Bhakra Nangal Dam has developed a tilt of 1.77 inches. The video misleadingly claims that a breach in the dam could cause flooding in several cities, including Delhi. The Fact Check Unit of the Press Information Bureau (PIB) has clarified that the claim is false and noted that the actual recorded deflection of the dam wall on 27th August 2024 was 0.86 inches. PIB further stated that the dam’s stress, strain, pore pressure and seepage parameters are all within the prescribed permissible limits and the Dam is completely safe. PIB also urged people not to believe or circulate sensational claims that can create unnecessary fear and panic.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will share his thoughts with the people of the country and abroad in the Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani at 11 AM on Sunday. It will be the 137th episode of the monthly radio programme. The programme will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani and Doordarshan network, the AIR News website, and the Newsonair mobile app. It will also be live-streamed on the YouTube channels of AIR News, DD News, the PMO, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Akashvani will broadcast the programme in regional languages immediately after the Hindi broadcast.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that India is fast emerging as a global platform for manufacturing, innovation and exports. She urged Canadian investors to tap the country’s growing potential to serve both domestic and international markets. She said, India’s reform-led transformation and strong growth trajectory are creating opportunities for a more resilient and investment-driven India-Canada economic partnership.Addressing a high-level Business Roundtable in Toronto yesterday, Sitharaman highlighted that reforms, digitalisation, infrastructure investment and targeted policy support were steadily strengthening the environment for long-term investment in the country. She invited Canadian companies and investors to view India not merely as an investment destination, but as a strategic partner and platform for global growth. She encouraged businesses to establish long-term operations and partnerships that can serve both the Indian market and international markets.The Finance Minister also highlighted opportunities for Canadian companies in financial services, particularly through the Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City) International Financial Services Centre (GIFT IFSC).  With ambition to raise two-way trade to 70 billion dollar annually by 2030, Sitharaman emphasised that the India-Canada economic opportunity extends far beyond trade, encompassing investment, technology, innovation, financial services and long-term global partnerships.

. Ahead of Independence Day, a platform for creative expression has been provided to the youth in Uttar Pradesh. For this, the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign was launched. Under this campaign, the graffiti wall programme organised near Lucknow University today. Artists from the city painted public murals on the theme of a mafia-free and changing Uttar Pradesh. Through these paintings, the Uttar Pradesh of before 2017 and the changes that have taken place in Uttar Pradesh thereafter were portrayed.On the wall, artists used their colours and imagination to portray in paintings the changed positive environment in the state in terms of law and order, infrastructure and opportunities for youth. Young painter Manish Saroj’s painting expressed the pain of Uttar Pradesh suffering under mafia rule before 2017, while also presenting a positive picture of the change taking place now.Under the campaign, a comic distribution and dialogue programme will be organised in Muzaffarnagar tomorrow. During this, an original comic based on communal harmony will be distributed. Along with this, dialogues will also be held with youth in schools. On August 14, the song ‘Azadi from Fear’ of the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign will be launched. It will also feature a confluence of rap, music and digital art.

. The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana has completed 12 years today, marking a significant milestone in transforming the country’s financial inclusion landscape. The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on this day in 2014. Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, more than 59 crore accounts have been opened so far, with total deposits amounting to 3 lakh 17 thousand crore rupees.As the world’s largest financial inclusion initiative, the scheme continues to redefine access to banking for all Indians. The average deposit per account is 5,356 rupees. Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, 78 per cent of the accounts have been opened in rural or semi-urban areas, and approximately 56 per cent of accounts are owned by women. Over 41 crore RuPay cards have been issued to Jan Dhan account holders. The scheme has also empowered millions, particularly the marginalised sections, to access banking and financial services to improve their socio-economic conditions.The Jan-Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity, with Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana at its core, has proven to be a diversion-proof mechanism for the direct delivery of financial assistance. Due to initiatives like Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, India’s Financial Inclusion Index has risen from 53.9 in 2018 to 67 in 2026, showcasing deeper access to credit, insurance, savings and digital payments. As the world’s largest financial inclusion initiative, the scheme is redefining access to banking for millions of underprivileged citizens.

. The Indian women’s hockey team ended their FIH World Cup campaign with a historic 3-1 win over higher-ranked Germany in the fifth-place classification match at Amstelveen, Netherlands, yesterday. The fifth-place finish is India’s best performance at the World Cup in 52 years, since the team finished fourth in the inaugural edition in 1974. The achievement is even more impressive, as the current squad included 11 World Cup debutants. For India Ishika opened the scoring in the 43rd minute, followed by two quick goals from Navneet Kaur in the 44th and 47th minutes.Germany’s Lynn Krings scored a late consolation goal in the 59th minute. India lost only one match in the tournament, going down 0-2 to hosts and Olympic champions the Netherlands. The team also drew with China and England and defeated South Africa 6-1. After being eliminated from the semi-final race following a goalless draw against Australia, India bounced back strongly against Germany. Despite a slow start, India scored three goals in four minutes and defended firmly against Germany’s attacks. The performance will give the team a major confidence boost ahead of next month’s Asian Games in Japan.

. The death toll from devastating flash floods in Nepal-Tibet has risen to 469, while 1,545 people remain missing on both sides of the border. Rescue teams are searching riverbanks and isolated settlements for survivors and recovering bodies swept downstream. However, concerns remain over a newly formed barrier lake near the source of the Bhote Koshi river system. Authorities fear that a breach could trigger another surge of water, worsening the disaster and hampering rescue operations. Nepalese security personnel have evacuated more than 800 people from the affected districts.

. A magnitude 5.1 earthquake struck Sichuan province in southwestern China today, prompting a fresh flood alert in Nepal. Authorities ordered evacuations in the Trishuli area amid fears of rising river levels. Nepal Police said a water dam on the Tibet side had burst again and urged residents, security personnel and rescue workers to move to safer locations. Road construction between Trishuli and Rasuwa has also been suspended, with heavy machinery withdrawn as water levels rose. Residents have described losing homes, shops and belongings after floodwaters surged through the Trishuli and Dhobi river areas, forcing them to flee. Rescue operations are continuing despite difficult terrain and weather conditions.

. In Men’s Cricket, the second and final Test between India and Sri Lanka ended in a draw, with the hosts at 429 for 9 in their second innings on the fifth and final day in Colombo.Despite the draw, the Shubman Gill-led side clinched the two-match series 1-0.Batting first in the second Test, India declared at 503 for 9 before bowling Sri Lanka out for 290 to secure a 213-run first-innings lead. The visitors enforced the follow-on, but Sri Lanka showed remarkable resilience in their second innings. They reached 429 for 9, taking a lead of 216 runs, before both captains agreed to call off the match.

. Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri today said that country is not merely a participant in the global energy landscape but is increasingly shaping it as the world’s third-largest consumer of energy and oil. The Minister said that India is the third-largest refiner and fourth-largest LNG importer. He said this while interacting with senior officers of the Indian Foreign Service.In a social media post, Mr Puri said that the country’s energy demand is expected to grow 2.5 times by 2047, accounting for around 25 percent of incremental global demand. The Minister underlined that transformative reforms have strengthened domestic capabilities, diversified energy sources, deepened strategic partnerships and accelerated country’s transition towards cleaner energy over the past decade under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

. Raksha Bandhan, the festival of the special bond between brothers and sisters, is being celebrated today across the country. On this occasion, sisters tie colourful Rakhi around the wrist of their brothers and pray for their prosperity, health and well-being. In return, brothers pledge to protect and support their sisters and present them gifts.President Droupadi Murmu has conveyed her greetings to all Indians living in the country and abroad on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan today. In her message on social media, the President said that the sacred tradition of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of Indian culture and spiritual traditions since ancient times. The President said that over time, Raksha Bandhan has become a cherished social festival, symbolising the bond of love and protection between brothers and sisters.She said the festival strengthens feelings of affection, respect and mutual responsibility among siblings, friends, families and different sections of society. President Murmu said Raksha Bandhan reminds that the foundation of every relationship in life rests on trust, sensitivity and mutual cooperation. The President called upon the people to resolve, on this occasion, to protect society and the nation, and to move forward with the same spirit towards building a developed India.Vice President CP Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have greeted the people on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan today. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan wished that the joyous occasion strengthens the bonds of love, affection and togetherness, and inspires everyone to uphold the values of compassion, harmony and mutual respect.He also wished happiness, peace and prosperity to everyone. Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed hope that the festival of Raksha Bandhan brings happiness, prosperity and success to everyone’s lives. He also wished that the bond of love, affection and mutual trust remains strong and unbreakable forever.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has extended greetings to countrymen on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said the festival celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolises India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.The Lok Sabha Speaker added that Raksha Bandhan is not merely a festival of tying a sacred thread of protection but is a celebration of trust, respect, love, and the lifelong commitment to stand by one another. He said that the bond between a brother and sister is considered one of the purest relationships in the world, as there is neither selfishness nor any condition attached to this relationship.He underlined that in India’s culture, the meaning of protection is not limited merely to ensuring the safety of sisters but also represents a commitment to protecting the respect, dignity, rights, and dreams of women. The Lok Sabha Speaker emphasised that when every daughter and every sister in society is safe, respected, and able to move forward with confidence, the nation will become truly stronger and more empowered. He urged everyone to take the resolve to always preserve love, trust, and open communication within families.

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said that the country today stands as an important place of transformation and renewed confidence, showcasing the results of collective determination and efforts. The Vice President said this after releasing a book titled Sankalp Se Siddhi ka Modi Yug written by Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari. He said that whether it is advancing technology, building modern infrastructure, and strengthening national unity and promoting women-led development, education is the tool for empowerment. Mr Radhakrishnan also highlighted the contributions of the country’s youth, women, farmers, workers, and every citizen for their involvement in building a stronger and prosperous nation. He also underlined that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the only leader in the world to provide free Covid-19 vaccines not only to 140 crore Indian people but also to hundred more countries.Speaking about the book, the Vice President said that through the publication, the author seeks to bring together many aspects of country’s larger narratives, reviving pride in cultural heritage and enhancing the country’s voice at the global stage. He added that the book reflects the journey of the nation and encourages everyone and boosts their enthusiasm.

. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan today celebrated Raksha Bandhan with school children at Uprashtrapati Bhavan. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan said that Raksha Bandhan symbolises the beautiful bond of love, trust and protection.

. In Men’s Cricket, hosts Sri Lanka were 163 for two against India in their second innings of the Colombo Test, when reports last came in. India enforced the follow-on after bowling Sri Lanka out for 290 in their first innings. Resuming the penultimate day at 265 for 8, Sri Lanka managed to add only 25 runs.All-rounder Sonal Dinusha struck his second consecutive century, scoring 103 runs. For India, Prasidh Krishna and Manav Suthar took three wickets each, while Saransh Jain claimed two wickets.India declared their first innings at 503, powered by centuries from Dhruv Jurel and Devdutt Padikkal. India is currently leading the two-match series 1-0.

. The first Kanda Express carrying over 450 tonnes of onions from Nashik, Maharashtra, has reached Delhi early this morning. The Consumer Affairs Ministry said that the government has undertaken a calibrated and targeted release of buffer stocks to ensure adequate availability and support price stability during the seasonal demand period. The Ministry said that the Kanda Express initiative has emerged as an effective logistics intervention for moving buffer onions from producing regions to consumption centres.The supplies are being moved through road transport to other major consumption centres, namely Chennai, Kolkata, Ernakulam, Guwahati, Varanasi, Lucknow, Patna, Chandigarh, Jammu and Amritsar. The Ministry informed that onion availability is comfortable to meet domestic demand in the coming months, supported by estimated production of over 307 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. The retail sale of onions at 35 rupees per kilogram was launched yesterday through mobile vans and retail outlets of NCCF and NAFED, as well as through Safal and Kendriya Bhandar outlets.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today met a group of 21 pilgrims belonging to Tamil Nadu in New Delhi who were rescued from Nepal. The pilgrims had arrived in Kathmandu from the flood-affected area yesterday and reached New Delhi this afternoon.In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar thanked the government of Nepal and its Army for the rescue efforts. He also appreciated the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu for facilitating their smooth return to India.Later, talking to media, Dr Jaishankar said that the Government of India is working to support Nepal in the relief and rescue of people following the flash flood. The Minister said that he spoke to the Nepalese Foreign Minister this morning and offered a range of support.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 1.9 per cent down at 1,58,386 rupees per 10 grams while, Silver slipped 1.9 per cent to 2,39,500 rupees per kilogram.
. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 14 paise to close at 95.55 rupees against the US dollar.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in negative territory today. The Sensex declined 539 points or 0.70 per cent to close at 76,934. The Nifty lost 117 points or 0.48 per cent to settle at 24,091. In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index and the Smallcap 100 index dipped 0.1 per cent each.Earlier, the markets opened on a positive note, supported by easing crude oil prices and hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough between Iran and Oman. However, both the indices soon gave up their early gains and slipped into negative territory. The indices remained largely range-bound through most of the session as selling pressure persisted due to Sensex monthly futures and options expiry. In the subsequent Closing Auction Session the indices extended their losses.In the Sensex pack, 24 out of 30 companies logged losses. Among the top underperformers, HDFC Bank slipped 2.1 per cent, NTPC declined two per cent and Mahindra and Mahindra lost 1.8 per cent. In contrast, Kotak Mahindra Bank advanced 1.7 per cent, ICICI Bank gained 0.9 per cent and Tech Mahindra added 0.8 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 20 out of 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top laggards, Midsmall Private Banks shed 2.6 per cent, PSU Bank lost 2.1 per cent and Bankex dropped 1.7 per cent. In contrast, Capital Goods gained 0.6 per cent, Telecommunication added half a per cent and Healthcare rose 0.4 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2 thousand 557 companies declined, 1 thousand 779 advanced and 190 remained unchanged.

. Global crude oil prices rose moderately today. Brent crude was trading 0.7 per cent up at 88 US dollars and 50 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.4 per cent up at 82 US dollars and 50 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has completed ten years of transforming digital payments and has emerged as the backbone of India’s digital payments ecosystem. The UPI, which was launched on 25th August 2016, has surged almost 13 thousand fold in transaction volume. The Finance Ministry said that the annual transaction volume expanded from just 1.78 crore transactions in 2016-17 to over 24 thousand 162 crore transactions in 2025-26. The transaction value also rose sharply from seven thousand crore to nearly 314 lakh crore during the same time period. The Ministry said that UPI has also emerged as a global platform for cross-border digital payments and is currently operational in 11 countries. These are United Arab Emirates, France, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Singapore, Mauritius, Qatar, Cambodia, Greece and Maldives.UPI has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, providing an interoperable, real-time payments platform. Today, it is the preferred mode of payment for millions of users, transforming the way India transacts. By bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation. The unprecedented scale and reliability achieved by UPI have received global recognition. It said, the International Monetary Fund has acknowledged it as the world’s largest real‑time payment system. As of 2025, UPI accounts for nearly 49 per cent of the world’s real-time payment transaction volume.

. The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has expanded the Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID)-based silver hallmarking ecosystem with 341 silver Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs) across 102 districts, and more than 25,000 silver jewellers are registered with BIS ahead of the festive season. The BIS informed that since the launch of the Silver HUID portal on 1 September last year, over 77 lakh silver jewellery pieces have already been hallmarked with HUID.The six-digit HUID under the Hallmarking System Assures Traceability of Silver Jewellery and Artefacts. The BIS advised consumers purchasing silver jewellery to look for the BIS hallmark and verify the HUID through the BIS CARE app. It also advised to purchase only hallmarked silver jewellery from BIS Registered Jewellers to be assured of its purity. Further, the BIS urged consumers to also obtain a proper invoice for the purchase of silver articles and retain it for future reference.

. Indian Grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa created history, becoming the first Indian to win the Grand Chess Tour after staging a stunning comeback to defeat defending champion Fabiano Caruana 15-13 in the final at St. Louis in the US last night. Praggnanandhaa started the final day six points behind Caruana but won both rapid games to take the lead.He then held his ground in the four blitz games to seal a 15-13 victory, claim 2 lakh dollar first prize and also secure a guaranteed spot in next year’s Grand Chess Tour. In the third-place match, Wesley So also made a strong comeback against Vincent Keymer. After the players shared the rapid games, So won all four blitz games to seal an 18-12 victory. Earlier, Praggnanandhaa had lost the first classical game to Caruana 6-0 but drew the second game 3-3, keeping his hopes alive.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman will be on a six-day visit to the United States beginning today. During her visit to the US, she will travel to Chicago, Asheville and New York. In Chicago, Finance Minister will participate in a Roundtable Conference with prominent investors and engage with leading CEOs, Presidents and senior representatives of the private sector. Bilateral one-to-one meetings with CEOs and senior leadership of select companies in Chicago will also be held.The discussions will focus on India’s investment opportunities, economic outlook and areas for strengthening business and investment partnerships between India and the United States. Ms Sitharaman will also visit the Polsky Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation at the University of Chicago, where she will exchange perspectives on entrepreneurship, innovation, technology commercialisation and strengthening linkages with India’s rapidly expanding startup and innovation ecosystem.The Finance Minister will also interact with members of the Indian community in Chicago during her visit. In Asheville, Ms Sitharaman will lead the Indian delegation at the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting under the United States Presidency of the G20. The meeting, scheduled for 31st August and 1st September, will bring together Finance Ministers, Central Bank Governors and senior economic officials from G20 members to deliberate on key global economic and financial issues. The meeting follows the G20 Finance and Central Bank Deputies Meeting scheduled for 29th and 30th August. The engagement will also provide an opportunity for India to advance its perspectives on contemporary global economic challenges and strengthen cooperation with G20 partners.In New York, Ms Sitharaman will participate in an Investor Roundtable with CEOs and senior representatives of leading New York-based companies. She will also hold one-to-one meetings with senior executives and CEOs from the financial sector to discuss investment opportunities, India’s economic and financial landscape, and avenues for strengthening financial and institutional linkages between India and the United States. During her visit to New York, NASDAQ, a pioneering global electronic marketplace and one of the world’s leading technology-driven financial market platforms, will host Ms Sitharaman in the bell-ringing ceremony. The visit will conclude on the 2nd of the next month.The finance minister is on a 9-day visit to Canada and the US, which began on August 25. In the first leg of her visit, Ms Sitharaman focused on strengthening India-Canada economic ties. In Canada, she attended the inaugural India-Canada Economic and Financial Dialogue in Toronto and also met investors and businesses from sectors including energy, artificial intelligence and critical minerals. The discussions focused on strengthening economic and financial cooperation and creating greater opportunities for investment and business between the two countries.

. Khelo India Dialogue programmes were held in various locations across Mizoram to encourage students and young athletes to pursue sports and improve their performance in line with changing times. As part of the initiative, Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the Khelo India Dialogue through video conferencing yesterday, outlining ways in which sports could contribute to the country’s development.Prime Minister Modi said sports should not be viewed merely in terms of winning medals but also as a means of building a stronger and more united India. He stressed the importance of regular physical exercise and urged participants to maintain a healthy mind and practise self-discipline. In Aizawl, the NSS Unit of Government Aizawl North College organised a programme where resource person Dr T. Lalremruata highlighted the importance of teamwork, unity and self-discipline in sports. A similar programme was held at Government Champhai College, where NSS Programme Officer Lalventluanga spoke about various opportunities for the development of students and athletes and interacted with the participants.In Hnahthial, the programme was organised at Government Higher Secondary School with the assistance of Khelo India Judo Instructor Zomuansanga. A total of 127 students, including 67 boys and 60 girls, took part in the event. At Government Saitual College, Khelo India Saitual District Representative Laltleipuia said children were being trained and encouraged to pursue sports under the Khelo India initiative. He said football and wrestling training for children was also being conducted intensively in Saitual district under the programme.

The Department of Pharmaceuticals has announced the second call for applications under the Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma and MedTech (PRIP) Scheme.The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers today said that the scheme with a financial outlay of five thousand crore rupees aims to strengthen India’s Pharma and MedTech research and development ecosystem by supporting startups, MSMEs, and large companies to leapfrog up the innovation value chain. Applications are invited across two tracks which are early stage and later stage.The Ministry said that the Application forms and supporting guidance are available on the PRIP portal.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has paid homage to Mahatma Ayyankali and Sree Narayana Guru on their birth anniversary today. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that Mahatma Ayyankali is remembered as a great pioneer of social justice. The Prime Minister added that his efforts to secure educational opportunities for the marginalised, improve the lives of agricultural workers and serve the poor remain very inspiring.Mr Modi also said that his life gives strength to all those working for social empowerment. He also called Sree Narayana Guru a towering social reformer, spiritual leader and thinker, who devoted his life to building a society rooted in dignity and compassion. Mr Modi said that Sree Narayana Guru’s thoughts gave strength to countless people and his focus on education and learning was equally noteworthy.Union Home Minister Amit Shah also paid tributes to Sree Narayana Guru and Mahatma Ayyankali on their birth anniversary. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that Sree Narayana Guru showed the path to build a more harmonious, and benevolent society through spirituality. Mr Shah said, his principles of knowledge, compassion, equality and spiritual freedom continue to inspire people. In another post, Mr Shah said that Mahatma Ayyankali was a pioneering social reformer who paved the way for social transformation through education in Keralam. He said, Mahatma Ayyankali also laid the foundation of a united and robust society upholding the values of social justice and equity.Defence Minister Rajnath Singh paid tribute to Mahatma Ayyankali. In a social media post, Mr Singh said that Mahatma Ayyankali devoted his life to fighting for the rights and dignity of the oppressed. The Minister said that Mahatma Ayyankali challenged social discrimination and strengthened the cause of equality and social justice in society. His life and legacy continue to inspire the collective pursuit of a more equitable and harmonious society, founded on equality, dignity and social justice.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. India’s Velavan Senthilkumar stormed into the final of the PSA Budapest Squash Open after a thrilling 3-2 victory over compatriot Veer Chotrani in the semifinals last night. Both Indian players advanced to the semifinals following impressive performances, as Chotrani defeated Egypt’s Mohamed El Sherbini 3-1, and Velavan secured a dominant 3-0 victory over Malaysia’s Eain Yow Ng. Velavan will now face local favourite and World No. 55 Balázs Farkas of Hungary in the final tonight. Farkas reached the final after a straight-games victory of 3-0 against Egypt’s Moustafa Elsirty.

The government has reiterated its commitment to reimagining skills, saying it is taking all measures to skill youth and prepare them for future growth with a vision to achieve Viksit Bharat by the year 2047. NITI Aayog released a report titled Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat@2047 which provides a blueprint for a skilling architecture.NITI Aayog said that in certain sections, the figure of 8.7 crore NEET youth has been misinterpreted as unemployed. It said that the category of NEET in the report refers to those not seeking employment and therefore, it cannot be read as a measure of joblessness or as an addition to the unemployment rate. NITI Aayog stressed that the Report has clearly said that the database utilised in computation of these figures is based on National Sample Survey, NSS 78th Round which was collected during the COVID-19 pandemic.

. Grand Master Trilok Subba from Sikkim has been selected to represent India at the World Taekwondo Poomsae Championship. Akashvani correspondent reports that internationally acclaimed Taekwondo player Grand Master Trilok Subba, from Sikkim, has been selected to represent India at the World Taekwondo Poomsae Championship in Chuncheon, South Korea.The Championship is scheduled to take place from 16th to 20th September. Subba will compete in the Under-60 Male Individual Poomsae and team events in the Senior category. Prior to this selection, Subba clinched a gold medal for the National Team at the National Taekwondo Poomsae Championship held in Maharashtra in July 2026. Mr Subba will leave Sikkim shortly to join the National Camp in Maharashtra & then he will travel to South Korea for the Championship.

. India’s double Olympic medallist Neeraj Chopra has qualified for the 2026 Diamond League final, which will be held in Brussels next month. Chopra accumulated 12 points in the standings. Chopra had finished fourth at the Doha meet in June with a throw of 85.69 metres before recording a season-best 88.05 metres at the Lausanne meet earlier this month, where he finished second. Chopra is sixth in the standings after competing in two Diamond League meets this season. Chopra’s two performances were enough to secure a place in the Diamond League final.

. Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa cruised into the finals of the Grand Chess Tour’s last leg after 19-9 win over Germany’s Vincent Keymer. Having won the second Classical game, the Indian enjoyed a huge lead of six points coming into the final day on which games of shorter duration were played.He defeated Keymer in back-to-back rapid encounters to nearly seal his spot in the finals taking an unassailable 17-3 lead before another victory in the first game of blitz took his points tally to 19.Pragnanandhaa will take on pre-event favourite and defending champion Fabiano Caruana of the USA States in the event finale.The top three finishers will automatically qualify for next year’s Grand Chess Tour.
